scenes.headline: Opening a website was enough
scenes.say: Outdated iPhone or Android? Opening one website was enough to get robbed.

scenes.headline: Real websites, poisoned
scenes.body: Sekoia links it to Russia's APT29, with “moderate to high confidence”.
scenes.say: Security firm Sekoia says hackers it links to Russia's APT29 planted attack code on real websites and fake lookalikes.

scenes.headline: One hijacked analytics script
scenes.body: Plerdy's tracker carried the code, August 27 to September 3.
scenes.say: They also hijacked an analytics script called Plerdy for about a week, so sites using it passed the attack on.

scenes.headline: Cookies, messages, Wi-Fi passwords
scenes.body: The code checked each phone first, then picked an attack.
scenes.say: The code checked each phone first. Outdated ones lost browser cookies, and some lost messages, photos and Wi-Fi passwords.

scenes.headline: Apple fixed one bug in May 2024
scenes.body: CISA flagged it as exploited on November 4.
scenes.say: Apple fixed one of these bugs in May 2024. On November fourth, the US agency CISA flagged it as exploited.

scenes.headline: Every bug was already patched.
scenes.body: Sekoia: an up-to-date system is safe.
scenes.say: Analyst note: no zero-days here. Every bug was already patched, and Sekoia says an up-to-date system is safe.

scenes.headline: Do this tonight
items: iPhone: Settings, then General, then Software Update
scenes.say: Tonight: on iPhone, open Settings, then General, then Software Update. On Android, update Chrome. And turn on automatic updates.

scenes.headline: The security story behind the headline.
scenes.say: Sources are in the description. Follow Securidge.
